This weekend, Helvetia & Bristol Firenze proudly presented Senza Fine: Janet I. Traub’s first official solo exhibition, featuring her Pomegranate Lovers series.



The exhibition unfolded within the historic Winter Garden, a space that has long served as a meeting place for artists, writers and travellers: a salon where ideas, creativity and cultural exchange flourished. Senza Fine reawakened this legacy, making the Winter Garden a living canvas for artistic dialogue.



Across the works, the symbolic image of the pomegranate guided a narrative of love, fragility and rebirth, reflecting the emotional universe of the artist and her return to painting after more than thirty years.Guests were invited into an immersive experience where painting, music and conviviality came together, transforming the space into a living moment of connection and exchange.



Thank you to everyone who joined us in bringing this chapter to life at Helvetia & Bristol.

A look into my editing process 🎨



I truly LOVE shooting on an analog camera and I love the look of film above everything else. However, the process of buying, shooting, developing, and waiting for film can be a challenge and it can get quite expensive. Over the last couple of years I’ve been experimenting with recreating a timeless film look that I can apply to my digital photos. And today I want to share it with you!



It will never replace film, but I thought it could be a good alternative for anyone who loves the aesthetic but doesn’t always want to go through the hassle of shooting film :)



I created a tutorial where I show you how I apply this film look to my own digital work and you can find that same Lightroom preset along with a few of my RAW files to practice with over on my Patreon. I’ll be diving deeper into little tricks and tips over the summer since I’ve really been enjoying putting on my education hat these past months and sharing more of what I’ve learned along my creative journey! 🎩

New YouTube video about compositions is up! 🍰



Recently I have been reflecting a lot on how I see the world and how that translates into my creative process and expression. I found myself going down a rabbit hole of my relationship with compositions and why I frame the things in the way I do.



I took all those thoughts and put them into a video and maybe it will help you uncover something about your own artistic inclinations. Had a lot of fun putting this together, if that sound interesting to you, the video is up on channel or you can find it through the link in my bio 🍰 😌 🎬

Do you ever think of an idea and then eventually start thinking your way out of it? “It’s silly” “It won’t work” “It’s not even that great of an idea” I’ve had this happen way too many times. Through meditation, therapy, and I guess just growing older, I’m trying to observe my thoughts more. And I’ve learned that if you want a different result from old patterns, you have to consciously break them and not give in to your default behaviour.

 

So, I decided to act on my idea without overthinking it and this short film was born. Please go act on your cool ideas! The world needs them more than ever, and you also need it for your inner child to be happy. Go allow yourself to make things just because you want to make them :)
isn’t there an irony in how we learn the same lessons over and over again, but life just packages them slightly differently each time

📍Carinzia e Stiria sono due regioni austriache diverse tra loro, vicinissime all’Italia e decisamente sottovalutate.

In quattro giorni si passa dalle acque turchesi del Wörthersee alle colline ricoperte di vigneti della Stiria , dalle terme più iconiche del Paese a piccoli produttori che raccontano il territorio.



Partiamo 👉🏽



🗓️ Giorno 1: arrivo a Klagenfurt, in Carinzia



Il modo migliore per iniziare il viaggio?

Check-in e giro in battello sul lago Wörthersee tra acque turchesi, ville storiche e paesini sul lago.



Il battello fa diverse tappe lungo il tragitto, e si può decidere dove scendere.

Pörtschach è un bellissimo stop, per fermarsi a fare aperitivo vista lago! 🌅

🗓️ Giorno 2: visita di Klagenfurt, una città elegante.



Ecco le principali cose da vedere a Klagenfurt in mezza giornata:

🏰 Landhaus Klagenfurt – Storico palazzo rinascimentale con la suggestiva Sala degli Stemmi.

⛪ Duomo di Klagenfurt – Cattedrale seicentesca con interni barocchi.



🥨 Il mercato Benediktinermarkt di Klagenfurt è il posto perfetto per assaggiare la cucina locale.

Qui si respira davvero la vita quotidiana della città.

un cafe molto buono con posti a sedere dentro e fuori
